metadata.title: Path-Addressable Context Layers: Multi-Level Disclosure for Long-Running LLM Agents

issues.title: Results section is entirely placeholder; no numbers reported
issues.quote:
Flat window (B1)       & \todo{--} & \todo{--} & \todo{--} \\
        Vector RAG (B2)        & \todo{--} & \todo{--} & \todo{--} \\
        MemGPT paging (B3)     & \todo{--} & \todo{--} & \todo{--} \\
        Self-RAG (B4)          & \todo{--} & \todo{--} & \todo{--} \\
        \midrule
        \textbf{\textsc{Structure}} & \textbf{\todo{--}} & \textbf{\todo{--}} & \textbf{\todo{--}}
issues.explanation: Both the main-results table (Table 2) and the ablation table (Table 3) contain only \todo{--} cells; the rating sweep, GC sweep, glance-to-detail analysis, path-locality, scalability, and qualitative example are all unfilled. The paper makes empirical claims throughout the abstract, intro, and method that no row of Section 6 substantiates. In the current state the manuscript is not a results paper.

issues.title: Abstract carries a visible \todo{Quantitative headline} marker
issues.quote: \todo{Quantitative headline: report token reduction, success-rate gain, and latency on the target benchmarks.}
issues.explanation: The abstract ends with a red-text TODO instructing the author to fill in the headline numbers. In submission the \todo macro renders red bracketed text in the PDF. This single line is sufficient for desk-reject in any peer-reviewed venue. Conclusion (sections/conclusion.tex:7) carries the equivalent placeholder.

issues.title: Limitations describes a strictly smaller benchmark scope than Experiments
issues.quote: Our benchmarks (AgentBench, WebArena, LongBench-Agent) cover English tool-use, web interaction, and long-document question answering. We do not evaluate code-generation agents, multi-lingual agents, or embodied agents.
issues.explanation: Experiments §Datasets explicitly adds SWE-bench (a code-generation agent benchmark), AppWorld (interactive coding), OSWorld (multimodal desktop), tau-bench, GAIA, WorkArena, BFCL-v4, AgentBoard, RULER, HELMET, LOFT, LoCoMo, and LongMemEval. The Limitations paragraph therefore directly contradicts the planned evaluation: the manuscript both claims to cover code agents (in §Datasets / Table 1) and disclaims them (in §Limitations).

issues.title: Backbone model, step cap N, and token budget B are unspecified
issues.quote: We evaluate with a frontier chat model as the agent backbone. \todo{Specify exact model, e.g., GPT-4.1 or Claude Sonnet, plus temperature, top-$p$, and context window.} ... We cap each trajectory at \todo{$N$} steps and a token budget of \todo{$B$} per run to prevent runaway loops.
issues.explanation: Three central reproducibility knobs — backbone model and decoding parameters, step budget, and token budget — are still TODO placeholders. Without these, none of the comparisons against B1–B4 are reproducible and the latency claims in §Conclusion / §Method are uninterpretable.

issues.title: Sub-10 ms retrieval claim asserted in abstract and intro without measurement
issues.quote: the system sustains sub-10\,ms retrieval over hundreds of entries via in-memory caches and HNSW indices
issues.explanation: The same number reappears in §Implementation Notes as 'reduces warm path lookups from roughly 500 ms to under 10 ms.' Both are presented as system properties, not as measurements drawn from a benchmark. There is no scalability table, no histogram, and Results §Scalability is a TODO. A reviewer cannot tell whether 'sub-10 ms' is a single anecdote or a sustained property; the headline claim must be backed by a plot or table or it should be removed from the abstract and introduction.

issues.title: Three bibliography entries use 'and others' placeholder author lists
issues.quote: author  = {Ye, Rui and others},   ...   author  = {Xu, Siyuan and others},   ...   author  = {Zhang, Yuxiang and others},
issues.explanation: AgentFold (ye2025agentfold), AgentDiet (xu2025agentdiet), and Memory-as-Action (zhang2025memact) all carry placeholder 'and others' author lists. These are concurrent works the paper depends on for positioning. Submitting with abbreviated author metadata risks an EIC bibliographic-quality flag and, more concretely, misattributes credit on works the paper directly compares itself against.

issues.title: Rating-blend formula mixes scales without a normalization scheme
issues.quote: a convex combination $s = \alpha \cdot s_\text{sim} + (1 - \alpha) \cdot \bar r$ blends semantic similarity $s_\text{sim}$ with the rating mean, where $\alpha \in [0, 1]$
issues.explanation: Cosine similarity $s_\text{sim}$ is in $[-1,1]$ (or in $[0,1]$ for normalized embeddings, depending on the index), while $\bar r$ is explicitly bounded in $[-1,1]$ (Method §source eval). The convex combination is only well-defined when both terms live on the same scale. The paper does not state which similarity normalization is assumed, nor whether ratings are rescaled before blending. The default $\alpha=0.7$ is therefore not a comparable hyperparameter across embedding indices (384/768/1024/1536).

issues.title: RQ3 and ablation A5 conflate substrate (audit log) with active mechanisms
issues.quote: \textbf{RQ3.} Which of the five mechanisms --- path addressing, multi-level disclosure, source evaluation, event-level garbage collection, or the audit-log feedback --- contributes most to the gains?
issues.explanation: The audit log is the substrate that backs reproducibility and replay; A5 ('No audit replay': events are no longer persisted as an ordered log) does not measure a mechanism that produces task-accuracy gains. It measures whether the agent can re-read prior context. Treating it as a fifth ablation against the accuracy/token Pareto frontier conflates infrastructure with reasoning machinery and risks an unfair-by-design ablation row. Either reframe A5 as a reproducibility-only artifact (and drop it from RQ3) or describe a concrete agent-level path through which 'no audit log' should hurt accuracy.

issues.title: Glance staleness corner case unaddressed
issues.quote: out = {"path": self.path, "glance": self.glance or self.content[:50]} ... The disclosure method lives on the entry itself, so an agent can scan hundreds of glances in a single prompt and pay for full content only where it is warranted.
issues.explanation: Listing 2 falls back to truncating self.content when self.glance is null. The Method text claims the projections are 'always consistent with the stored state', but if self.glance is precomputed (e.g., LLM-generated summary) and self.content is later updated through update(), the precomputed glance becomes stale. The paper does not specify whether glance is recomputed on update, invalidated, or treated as a snapshot. A reviewer who has worked on materialized summaries will flag this immediately.

issues.title: Replay determinism vs. denormalized rating aggregate is asserted but not derived
issues.quote: Each call emits a \textsc{context.rated} event and updates a denormalised pair $(\text{rating\_sum}, \text{rating\_count})$ on the entry, from which the mean $\bar r$ is derived. ... Because ratings are event-sourced, the per-step state is reproducible: replaying events up to step $t$ reconstructs the exact $\bar r$ the agent saw at that step.
issues.explanation: The exactness of the replay claim depends on (a) idempotent application of context.rated events to (rating_sum, rating_count), (b) deterministic event ordering, and (c) starting replay from a known seed state. The paper does not say which of these is enforced. Floating-point summation order matters numerically; if the denormalized aggregate is updated in receive order while replay reorders by event sequence, the reconstructed $\bar r$ will differ at the last bit. State the invariants or weaken the claim from 'exact' to 'approximate'.

issues.title: Five-contribution list mixes primitives, mechanisms, implementation, and release artifact
issues.quote: We formalise \emph{path-addressable multi-level disclosure} ... We introduce two mechanisms ... We implement \textsc{Structure} as an event-sourced orchestration platform ... We evaluate the system on long-horizon agent tasks ... We release the implementation, benchmark harness, and configurations
issues.explanation: The five-bullet list mixes a primitive (path-addressable multi-level disclosure), two mechanisms (rating, GC), an implementation, an evaluation, and a release. The first two are research contributions; the last three are reproducibility artifacts. EIC and reviewers in NLP venues frequently down-weight contribution lists that count engineering deliverables as scientific contributions. Compress to two or three actual contributions and move implementation/release to an Artifacts paragraph or Reproducibility statement.

issues.title: GC predicate precedence not parenthesized in prose
issues.quote: An event $e$ of type $\tau$ with step index $t_e$ is kept iff $\Pi(\tau).\text{pin}$ is true, or $t - t_e \leq \Pi(\tau).\text{steps}$ and $(\text{now} - e.\text{created\_at}) \leq \Pi(\tau).\text{seconds}$.
issues.explanation: The intended grouping is 'pin OR (steps_ok AND seconds_ok)' (a pinned event is always kept, otherwise both budgets must be satisfied). Without parentheses, a careful reader can also parse it as '(pin OR steps_ok) AND seconds_ok'. The math display following gc(E, t, Pi) does not pin the precedence either. Convert to a (pin) OR (steps AND seconds) display equation.

issues.title: Symbol B is overloaded: token budget vs. baseline labels B1..B4
issues.quote: The agent's objective is a task-defined reward $R$ under a total token budget $B$. ... \textbf{(B1) Flat window.} ... \textbf{(B2) Vector RAG.} ... \textbf{(B3) MemGPT paging.} ... \textbf{(B4) Self-RAG.} ... a token budget of \todo{$B$} per run
issues.explanation: The same letter B is used both as a scalar (token budget) and as a name prefix for baselines. The clash becomes visible in §Experiments §Implementation Details: 'a token budget of B per run' sits next to 'B1..B4'. Choose a different symbol for the token budget (e.g., $T$ or $\mathcal{B}_{\text{tok}}$) or rename the baselines to avoid the collision.

issues.title: Disclosure size budgets are stated without justification
issues.quote: a \textsc{glance} (one-line summary, $\leq 50$\,B), an \textsc{overview} (structured metadata and tags, $\approx 1$\,KB), and a \textsc{detail} (full content, optionally S3-backed)
issues.explanation: The two byte budgets are central to the token-cost story (an agent 'scans hundreds of glances in a single prompt') yet they appear as defaults rather than as derived numbers. Either anchor them ('chosen so that 200 glances fit within a 16k window') or move them to a parameters table.

issues.title: Default alpha = 0.7 chosen without reported sensitivity
issues.quote: $\alpha \in [0, 1]$ is a per-query hyperparameter defaulting to $\alpha = 0.7$
issues.explanation: 0.7 is presented as the default but the rationale is left to the §Rating sweep, which is a TODO. Either declare 0.7 as 'tuned on dev' or as 'chosen by inspection' so a reviewer is not left guessing.

issues.title: GC default policy described as 'roughly the width of a single plan-act cycle' but TTL values vary 2-10
issues.quote: gives tool calls and results a short step-TTL of roughly the width of a single plan--act cycle ... Default policy (Appendix, Table~\ref{tab:tools})
issues.explanation: The prose summary is 'roughly the width of a single plan-act cycle', but Table 4 (the actual policy) shows tool.call=3, tool.error=6, agent.thinking=2, agent.plan.step=4, run.state.change=8, task.* (non-complete)=6-10. That is a 5x range, not 'roughly one cycle'. Either tighten the prose or state the heterogeneity explicitly.

issues.title: Listings 1-2 use figure+verbatim instead of an ACL-conventional listing/algorithm float
issues.explanation: Two of the paper's three concrete code artifacts (Listing 1 and Listing 2) are typeset as figure floats wrapping verbatim text. ACL papers conventionally use lstlisting/algorithm/algorithmic, which adds keyword highlighting and a proper listing counter. The current form is acceptable but loose, and the captions read 'Listing X' while the float counter is 'Figure X'.

issues.title: Extended battery (BFCL, AgentBoard, LOFT, GAIA, WorkArena) unaccounted for
issues.quote: Running the full grid is not strictly required for the main claim; we identify a \emph{core} subset (Table~\ref{tab:datasets}) and treat the remainder as an extended battery reported in the appendix.
issues.explanation: The text promises 'extended battery in the appendix' but the appendix has no extended-battery table; only Hyperparameters and Infrastructure paragraphs (both TODO) and the Tools table. Either drop the cited but un-evaluated benchmarks (BFCL, AgentBoard, LOFT, GAIA, WorkArena) from §Experiments or commit to an appendix subsection that holds them.
